Single-target and dual-target CDR approaches are often hindered by the limitations of requiring at least one well-supplied domain. To address this challenge, we introduce a novel framework called Multi-Sparse Domain Recommendation (MSDR), which focuses on multi-target CDR across diverse domains with varying levels of richness. Unlike traditional methods, MSDR is specifically designed to tackle extreme sparsity in all relevant domains by: (a) enabling information sharing among related domains, regardless of their data density; and and (b) leveraging the unique information from indifferent domains to enrich the representation of under-represented domains. The key innovation of MSDRA lies in a new technical called the Multi-Sparse Domain Attention (MSDAttention) mechanism, which achieves selective information sharing through tailored technique that: (a) allows related domains to share information at a uniform level, and (b) allows indifferent domains to share information based on the uniqueness of their content. AR at the Max-Planck Institute for Plasma Physics in Germany is designed to investigate how plasma interacts with radio frequency waves. A plasma source with a 0.1 meter length and 0.5 meter diameter provides plasma necessary for the experiment, and features a helical antenna to produce high-density plasma in the helicon mode of discharge. Until now, it was unclear if this plasma source could effectively produce plasma in the helicon mode, especially given its short length which is not ideal for helicon plasma generation. A study using a 1-Tesla magnetic field and 10 kW input power found that this plasma source can indeed produce plasma in the helicon mode, as it meets all necessary criteria: it is longer than the helicon plasma wavelength, has the right length to radius ratio, and its performance increases with length at the same power level. Nevertheless, it operates at higher beta values and lower plasma wavelengths compared to typical helicon plasma generators, indicating the presence of helicon plasma resonance.
